newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bergesen Q1 pre-tax hit by forex losses.
newsitem.headline: Bergesen Q1 pre-tax hit by forex losses.

text.p: Bergesen d.y. Group, Norway's largest shipping company, posted on Thursday first-quarter operating profits up 21 percent from a year ago and forecast an improved result for 1997 compared with 1996.
Bergesen booked an operating profit after depreciation of 228 million crowns against 189 million crowns in the same year-ago period.
Pre-tax profits were down 16 percent at 185 million crowns versus 221 million crowns due to a rise in the dollar exchange rate, which created an unrealised exchange rate loss of 44 million crowns.
Bergesen said net currency exchange losses amounted to 27 million crowns in the three month period against 29 million crown a year ago.
The 1996 figures were adjusted for the new accounting principle for drydocking expenses and the change in deferred tax due to the new tax regime for Norwegian shipping.
Bergesen said results from its major markets -- gas carriers and tankers -- improved, while profits for dry bulk vessels showed a small decline.

Operating profits for gas carriers rose 30 percent to 174 million crowns, versus 134 million crowns, with most gas segments showing an improvement compared with the corresponding year-ago period and the fourth quarter 1996, Bergesen said.
Tankers showed a rise in operating profits to 34 million crowns, against 25 million, as rates continued to improve.
"Limited availability of new tonnage, along with a positive trend in transport requirements for oil, were important factors," the company said in a statement releasing the results.
In the dry bulk division operating profits dipped to 16 million crowns compared with 19 million crowns.

Bergesen said it had drydocked four gas carriers and three tankers in the first three months. In aggregate it plans to drydock 31 vessels in 1997 -- 21 gas carriers, nine tankers and one dry bulk vessel.
It added that it expected to book a profit of 22 million crowns in the second quarter from the sale in April of the dry bulk vessel Larina.
For the full year Bergesen said it expected a better result for gas carriers and tankers than in 1996, while the dry bulk sector was forecast to remain in line with a last year.

"Based on the first quarter results the conditions favour somewhat improved profit for the gas carriers in 1997 as against 1996. However a weaker market is expected throughout the summer, while the prospects for the autumn look good," it said.
"The tankers are expected to show an improvement for the year 1997 compared with 1996."
